turns.prompt_text: I own petg filament for a 3D printer what kind of plate does it need to go on
turns.response_html:
PETG works best on a textured PEI plate or a glass bed coated with a release agent.

While it adheres strongly, it can fuse to smooth surfaces and damage them. Here is how to handle different plate types:

  • Textured PEI: The safest option; it sticks well when hot and pops off easily once cooled.
  • Glass or Smooth PEI: You must use a glue stick or hairspray as a "release layer" to prevent the PETG from permanently bonding to the surface.
  • Engineering Plate: Works well at bed temperatures around 70°C–80°C.

Would you like me to find the specific bed temperature settings for your printer model?
